name: Erdős–Straus conjecture
question: Can 4/n always be written as three positive unit fractions for every integer n at least two?
first_attack: Seek new modular covering identities and exact certificates

campaign.method: Modular covering identities with unit-fraction certificates
campaign.hypothesis: For every integer n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Find a polynomial identity family covering a residue class of primes not covered by the classical Mordell identities, and prove it symbolically.
campaign.next_experiment: Mine the certificate table for primes n = 1 mod 24, cluster solutions by (x mod n, divisor pattern) and propose parametric identities for symbolic verification.
campaign.falsification: An n together with a proof that no positive-integer triple exists; a finite search failure is not a counterexample.
campaign.blocker: Classical identities leave quadratic-residue classes uncovered, and known results show identities of the standard polynomial type cannot cover them all; a different idea is needed.

probes.name: Erdős–Straus conjecture
probes.title: Erdos-Straus unit-fraction certificates for every n up to N
probes.frontier: Known: computational verification is reported far beyond this range (at least 10^14 in the literature). Reproduction only.

smoke.scope: For every integer 2 <= n <= 20,000, explicit positive integers x <= y <= z with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx).

deep.scope: For every integer 2 <= n <= 1,000,000, explicit positive integers x <= y <= z with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx).

milestones.title: Erdos-Straus triples certified for every 2 <= n <= 20,000
milestones.scope: Finite range only; known computational verification is far larger
milestones.description: Explicit (x, y, z) with 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) for all 19,999 integers, each re-checked by exact integer arithmetic; the deep run covers n <= 10^6.

formal_statement.encodes: 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z cleared to 4xyz = n(xy + yz + zx) with x, y, z > 0.

kernel_checked.claim: Explicit positive solutions for every 2 ≤ n ≤ 100, re-checked by the kernel.
